Bempedoic acid and major cardiovascular events

Does bempedoic acid reduce major cardiovascular events in statin-intolerant patients? One trial answers this; the other three registrations on this page measure something else, and one of them is not a bempedoic acid trial.

Not applicable: one trial, so there is no between-study variance to estimate.

Nothing is pooled: one trial. This is not a withheld estimate -- the value stands and is clear Outcomes' own.

Why this pool stands. The estimate STANDS, and it is one trial's result rather than a synthesis -- which the card says, with k=1. HR 0.87 (0.79 to 0.96) is clear Outcomes' own registered Cox analysis, digit for digit, over its registered primary outcome: 'Number of Participants With First Occurrence of Four Component Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE)', defined by its registry record as 'death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or coronary revascularization, as assessed in a time-to first-event analysis'. Its counts are the registry's own: 819 of 6,992 against 927 of 6,978. And k=1 is correct rather than a shortfall. Of the four registrations this page includes, only clear Outcomes registers a cardiovascular-event primary. Clear Harmony's registered primaries are safety endpoints -- treatment-emergent adverse events and events of special interest, at 52 weeks. Clear Serenity's is percent change in ldl-c at week 12, a laboratory value. Neither can enter a MACE estimate, so leaving them out is right; what is missing is any statement that they were left out or why.

Three things a reader should know, none of which overturns the estimate. (1) one of the four included registrations is not a bempedoic acid trial at all. NCT02973841 is 'Sono-ease', a forty-patient device study of internal jugular vein cannulation whose registered primary outcome is 'complications rate'. It sits in this page's own include list. It carries no data record, so it touches no number here -- but it is the second wrong registration found in this corpus in one session, after NCT02583191 turned out to be a German treatment-satisfaction study on DOAC_CANCER_VTE. A registration that names an unrelated trial is invisible to every check that asks only whether an id is present and unique. (2) the published-comparison STEP compares this estimate against itself. The page's benchmark database holds exactly one entry for this outcome: 'clear Outcomes bempedoic acid vs placebo', Nissen 2023, HR 0.87 (0.79 to 0.96), k=1, n=13,970. That IS the trial whose result is on the card. A comparison of a number with itself agrees perfectly and establishes nothing, and the agreement should not be read as external corroboration. The honest denominator here is zero: no independent synthesis of this estimand is recorded on this page. (3) a single trial is not a synthesis. Nothing here is pooled, there is no heterogeneity to report, and the interval is clear Outcomes' own. The value of this page over reading the trial report is the provenance chain, not the statistics.

Authority it does not satisfyMecir C5/C7 (Mandatory conduct standards) -- criteria defined in advance. A post hoc derivation cannot discharge pre-specification, and precondition `criteria predefined` therefore fails for this topic, permanently and correctly.

Analysis set as the registry states itUp to 68 months. Registry results: 819 of 6,992 on bempedoic acid against 927 of 6,978 on placebo; Cox hazard ratio 0.87 (0.79 to 0.96). the only included registration with a cardiovascular-event primary

It carries no data record, so it touches no number here -- but it is the second wrong registration found in this corpus in one session, after NCT02583191 turned out to be a German treatment-satisfaction study on DOAC_CANCER_VTE. A registration that names an unrelated trial is invisible to every check that asks only whether an id is present and unique. (2) the published-comparison STEP compares this estimate against itself. The page's benchmark database holds exactly one entry for this outcome: 'clear Outcomes bempedoic acid vs placebo', Nissen 2023, HR 0.87 (0.79 to 0.96), k=1, n=13,970. That IS the trial whose result is on the card. A comparison of a number with itself agrees perfectly and establishes nothing, and the agreement should not be read as external corroboration. The honest denominator here is zero: no independent synthesis of this estimand is recorded on this page. (3) a single trial is not a synthesis. Nothing here is pooled, there is no heterogeneity to report, and the interval is clear Outcomes' own. The value of this page over reading the trial report is the provenance chain, not the statistics.
Why absentk=1 and nothing was pooled, so there is NO model call to quote, NO pooled estimate, NO heterogeneity and NO package version. This is not a missing artefact; it is the correct state for a topic with no synthesis.
Refusal discharges P46 becauseIt names what exists (one trial's own Cox interval), why no quotable model output can exist (nothing was pooled), and what would change it.
Background is now zero and it is computed0 background is the result of classifying 21 records, not an unfilled field. P17: a field whose name implies a check carries a computed value.
Why this is a correction not a relaxationIt moved counts in both directions across the corpus: sglt2-hf +10, bempedoic-acid-review -1. A loosening only ever adds. Four regression guards pin the negative case, including apixaban vs rivaroxaban where both arms are active.
K unscreened remainder noteWas 1 after the placebo-discriminator restatement; NCT05263778 screened 2026-08-19 and excluded on intervention -- it randomises a bempedoic acid/ezetimibe fixed-dose combination against placebo, so two agents differ between arms and no estimate is attributable to bempedoic acid. Population (post-ACS, not statin-intolerant) and outcome (LDL-C, not MACE) also fail and are named rather than relied on. Disposition at screening of remainder.bempedoic_newly_unscreened_2026_08_19.
And k5 is now zero which is a claimNO surfaced trial has bempedoic acid in every arm. That is a computed zero -- 21 records classified, 0 landing in background -- and not an empty field. It reads oddly for an add-on lipid agent and it is correct: the programme's non-experimental records are ACTIVE-COMPARATOR designs (bempedoic acid as the control against another agent), not background-therapy designs.
Refusal discharges P46 becauseIt names what was reached (one benchmark for this estimand), what was found insufficient (that benchmark IS the trial on the card, so the comparison would be the number against itself), and what would have to be obtained (an independent synthesis). The reason is a fact about the published evidence, not about our queue.
Why asked before deciding not to poolReading only registered primaries is how a poolable outcome one rank down goes unseen. Two of the three MACE-matching outcomes found here sit at secondary rank and a primaries-only screen would have missed both.
Three that are poolable but not eligibleThree trials report a MACE-matching outcome yet fail population or comparator. They could contribute a quantity but are out of scope, which is the opposite cell from the eleven eligible-but-not-poolable on sglt2-hf. Both cells are only visible under two axes.
Why this is stated rather than left implicitA rating of some concerns with no explanation reads as a judgement against the trial. Omitting the reason would manufacture a criticism exactly as a low-by-default manufactures a reassurance -- the same defect pointed the other way.
Registry facts backfilledRead from ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 on 2026-08-21. The judgements above were not revisited -- this adds the registry evidence beside a verdict that was made from it and did not record it, so a blind second assessor can be shown the same facts. A second assessment built on fewer facts is not a comparable assessment.
The allow list the rate is conditional onA disagreement rate is meaningless without the facts both assessors saw, so the list is stated here the way a denominator is stated. Fields emitted: trial, cohort, registered enrolment, registered masking, registered sites, registered comparator, number of registered arms, number of registered primary outcomes, registered primary outcome, registered analysis population, the rank the pooled result holds, the result being assessed, participants this review pools, registered enrolment minus participants pooled. Established by test, not argument: widening this list from 9 fields to 14 halved gepotidacin's disagreement -- its entire selection of the reported result divergence was a fact the second assessor had never been shown -- and left ceftaroline and tigecycline unmoved.
Which risk of bias domains drove the ratingWhere a result is rated worse than LOW overall, the domain carrying that judgement is: the randomisation process on 1 result(s), deviations from the intended intervention on 1 result(s), selection of the reported result on 1 result(s). The overall rating is the worst domain, so these are the domains that determine it.

The withholding question, asked at every rank

does this trial report, AT ANY RANK -- primary, secondary or other -- an outcome matching what the included trial reports as its primary?

Reading only registered PRIMARIES is how a poolable outcome one rank down goes unseen. Two of the three MACE-matching outcomes found here sit at SECONDARY rank and a primaries-only screen would have missed both.

Correction — NCT02666664

The recorded reason reads: 'its registered primaries are SAFETY outcomes -- treatment-emergent adverse events and events of special interest -- not cardiovascular events.' That is FACTUALLY WRONG. NCT02666664 registers THIRTEEN primary outcomes and the SECOND is 'Percentage of Participants With Adjudicated Major Adverse Cardiovascular Event'. It has a MACE primary.

How it happened: The object stores `registered_primary_measure` as a SCALAR holding ONE of the trial's thirteen primaries -- the first, TEAEs -- and the exclusion reason was written by characterising all primaries from that single value. A scalar field standing for a list is how the other twelve became invisible.

Verdict: EXCLUDE is still correct. The failing limb is POPULATION, not OUTCOME: this is CLEAR Harmony, in high-cardiovascular-risk patients on maximally tolerated statin therapy, whereas the review's population limb is statin-intolerant patients.

Class: A correct verdict reached by broken reasoning. It passed every outcome-based check because the outcome -- exclusion -- was right. Only reading the REASON against the registry caught it, and only because the withholding question is asked at every rank rather than at the primary alone.

Analysis output — ABSENT_AND_THAT_IS_THE_FINDING

k=1 and nothing was pooled, so there is NO model call to quote, NO pooled estimate, NO heterogeneity and NO package version. This is not a missing artefact; it is the correct state for a topic with no synthesis.

What stands instead: HR 0.87 (95% CI 0.79 to 0.96)
Provenance: CLEAR Outcomes' OWN registry-posted analysis, NOT a synthesis result computed here
Hazard Ratio (HR) 0.87, CI 0.79 - 0.96, statistical method Log Rank, p=0.004

Heterogeneity: Undefined: no between-study variance was estimated because no model was run.
What would change it: An estimand shared by two or more included trials. Where k is already above 1 and nothing pooled, the obstacle is the ESTIMAND rather than the evidence base, and this field must say which.

Published-meta comparison — PENDING_EXTERNAL_RESOLUTION

Denominator: —. The honest denominator here is ZERO, and that is a finding rather than a shortfall. The only benchmark this page holds for this estimand is CLEAR Outcomes itself -- the single trial whose result the card serves. A comparison of a number with itself agrees perfectly and establishes nothing, and that agreement must not be read as external corroboration. No INDEPENDENT synthesis of this estimand is recorded.

Explicitly not done: CITATION-STRING MATCHING. It would produce a comparison-shaped answer tonight and it is not identity: two syntheses citing the same trial under different labels would read as different, and the same label on different trials as the same. That is the substitution class this project audits for.
